---
title: "Run it yourself"
---

Everything runs in **R**, on your own laptop, with no network connection and no API
key.

## 1. Install R and RStudio

- **R 4.4 or later:** <https://cran.r-project.org>
- **RStudio Desktop:** <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>

## 2. Install the packages

Open RStudio and run:

```r
install.packages(c("arrow", "data.table", "ggplot2", "jsonlite", "lme4",
                   "rmarkdown", "knitr", "httr2"))
```

`arrow` is the one that sometimes gives trouble. If it fails, try:

```r
install.packages("arrow", type = "binary")
```

## 3. Get the materials

Either download the repository as a zip
([download](https://github.com/talking-to-machines/llmss-2026-workshops/archive/refs/heads/main.zip))
and unzip it, or clone it:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/talking-to-machines/llmss-2026-workshops.git
```

There is one folder per workshop:

| Folder | Workshop | Notebooks |
|---|---|---|
| `W1_aipop` | Workshop 1 · AIPOP: AI polling and MrP | 3 |
| `W2_twins` | Workshop 2 · The Wisdom of Digital Twins | 2 |
| `W3_audience` | Workshop 3 · The Silicon Audience: Silicon Voters | 1 |
| `W3_legal` | Workshop 3 · The Silicon Audience: Silicon Jury | 1 |

Each folder has its notebooks in `notebooks/`, numbered in the order you use
them, and everything they read in `data/`.

## 4. Check it works

In RStudio, set the working directory to one of the workshop folders (for
Workshop 1, simply open `W1_aipop/W1_aipop.Rproj`) and run:

```r
source("run_all.R")
```

It renders that workshop's notebooks in about a minute. If it ends with "All
notebooks rendered" (or "Output created"), you are ready.

Workshop 1's notebooks hand data from one to the next, so run them in order:
Notebook 2 writes the interviewed panel that Notebook 3 reads. A copy of that
panel is already in `W1_aipop/output/`, so Notebook 3 also runs on its own.

## Sending your own prompts (optional)

Some blocks send *your own* prompts to a model. Without a key they are
skipped and the notebook uses the stored answers. To run them, you need an
OpenAI API key. Put it in your `~/.Renviron` file (in RStudio:
`usethis::edit_r_environ()`), then restart R:

```
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key-here
```

The notebooks call `gpt-5-mini`. One full Silicon Voters Stage 3 run is
270 calls, a few cents at current prices.

## Exercises

The notebooks contain exercises with empty blocks (`# your code here`). The answer
keys are not part of the public materials, but you can ask for them: write to
